_comment: Metered ground truth for Sentinel-2 overpasses of the Stanford/EDF
single-blind controlled-release tests. This is the only dataset in the
project where the true emission rate is KNOWN rather than inferred from
another satellite's catalog, which makes it the correct instrument for
Rates are the metered 5-minute mean CH4 mass flow preceding the overpass,
in kg/h. Extracted from the papers' data repositories, NOT from the PDFs:
the papers publish only aggregates. The extraction was validated against
published SI Table S8 detection counts (28/28 cells match) and against
the papers' quoted extremes (7.2 [6.8, 7.6] t/h max; 1.4 [1.3, 1.5] t/h
PLATFORM IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: no source states S2A vs S2B. Resolve it
from the UTC timestamp against the Copernicus/GCS catalogue. The MGRS
tiles below are likewise unpublished; we resolved them ourselves and
citation: Sherwin, E.D. et al. (2023) Single-blind validation of space-based
point-source detection and quantification of onshore methane emissions.
Sherwin, E.D. et al. (2024) Single-blind test of nine methane-sensing
satellite systems from three continents. Atmos. Meas. Tech. 17:765-782.
data_sources: Zenodo archive of the 2022 deposit: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10149991
detection_limit_note: The widely quoted '1-3 t/h' is a vendor/literature figure in Sherwin 2023,
NOT a measurement from these tests. Empirically demonstrated: 1.4 t/h
(2021, 3 of 4 teams) and 1.05 t/h (2022, Orbio, to within +/-47%). The
authors call the smallest detected emission 'a rough upper bound on the
lower detection capabilities' and warn that the known-location design may
have boosted sensitivity beyond general practice. The 2022 campaign never
tested S2 between 0.005 and 1.05 t/h, so the floor is unconstrained there.

kind_semantics.release: metered non-zero release; compare our retrieved rate against kg_h
kind_semantics.zero_control: release rig present, metered ~zero; any flux we report is false
no_release: Stanford ran no release for these 2022 overpasses (SI S2.7 miscommunication).
The papers EXCLUDE them from all analysis. We treat them as additional zero
controls, which is OUR inference, not the papers': no release means no source.
Label them as such in any output.
kind_semantics.void: release cancelled mid-campaign; not a zero control, simply unusable
